scope: Gate B on the exact CMP-05 candidate bytes and live workbench at the locked treatment. This does not promote the component.

T1StripTest.evidence: With colour, movement and workbench copy mentally removed, the dot-screen likeness and controlled absence of ink on the matte remain recognisably the Mez halftone portrait rather than a generic avatar treatment.

T2ComponentRepetitionTest.evidence: The component owns one clipped image surface and no quote, profile or generic card anatomy. Repetition in the workbench exists only to prove allocation, range and failure states.

T3MotionComparisonTest.evidence: Two full-viewport screenshots sampled 1.04 video-seconds apart changed 37,050 of 101,124 pixels, or 36.64%, inside the live allocated portrait. The adjacent allocated static portrait changed 0 of 100,806 pixels.

T4RealContentTest.evidence: The locked treatment, range, allocation and failure states use the approved local matted portrait clips and a deliberate missing-source fixture; no fabricated likeness, remote fetch or placeholder portrait is present.

canonScan.notes: No gradients, glow, glass, ornamental motion, nested card anatomy or ungoverned network/runtime dependency were found. The only motion escape is the already recorded motion-policy=always exception, and it remains opt-in and offscreen-idled.

findings.location: invert attribute with baked light-plate matte
findings.finding: The inverted range example dots the baked plate and is materially weaker than the locked treatment.
findings.resolution: Keep this as a documented capability limitation. The locked treatment does not use invert; restoring it would require an alpha-channel media decision outside this gate.
